paras: The lynching of Sandy Wright was the shooting of a Black prisoner in the jail at Blakely, Early County, Georgia, by a party of masked men in late September 1881. Wright, whose first name was also printed as "Zandy" and "Andy," was serving a sentence for hog stealing when about a dozen men forced the jailer to surrender his key and killed him in his cell. The men were not identified, and the story spread from Georgia papers to a Chicago Tribune dispatch and editorial and to short items in weeklies across the country.

According to a special dispatch from Blakely to the Macon Telegraph and Messenger, Wright was serving a prison sentence for hog stealing that would have expired in about ten days. The same report said he "had a bad reputation" and had threatened during his imprisonment to kill several people, including the jailer, once he was released. The Atlanta dispatch repeated that claim, saying he had been heard to threaten the jailer and "several other residents of Early County."

The Blakely special, dated September 29, placed the attack "between the hours of 12 and 1 o'clock" the previous night. About a dozen masked men went to the jailer's residence and demanded the jail key, which he refused to give up until he was "compelled under the muzzles of pistols" to surrender it. One of the men stayed behind to guard the jailer at his house while the others went to the jail, opened it, and shot Wright to death with pistols in his cell. The detailed accounts place the killing inside the jail, so the jail was both where he was held and where he died.

The Atlanta dispatch reported that the names of none of the men were known and that there was "little hope" that any of them would ever be brought before the courts. The Blakely report closed by saying the affair was "greatly regretted by the quiet and peaceable citizens of Blakely." No report of an inquest, arrest or grand jury action appears in the coverage.

The fullest account reached print on October 1 in the Savannah Morning News, which reprinted the Macon Telegraph and Messenger's Blakely special in its column of Georgia news. That report set the victim's "bad reputation" and threats beside the regret of the town's "quiet and peaceable citizens," without naming any source for either claim. On October 3 the Chicago Daily Tribune ran a closely matching Atlanta dispatch under the headline "SHOT TO DEATH BY A MOB."

The Tribune also commented on the case in an editorial paragraph, remarking that it "required very little provocation" in "Earl County" to organize a masked mob and shoot a prisoner whose offense was stealing hogs. Weekly papers then carried the story as a single line in their news summaries. The Cambria Freeman in Pennsylvania said "Andy Wright" was "taken out and lynched Sunday morning," while a brief in the Huntsville Gazette called him "a colored desperado" who was "taken by a mob and shot." That brief reappeared in the Batesville Guard in Arkansas, the Iron County Register in Missouri and the Iola Register in Kansas between October 12 and 14, and the Crawford Avalanche in Michigan ran a condensed version of the Atlanta dispatch on October 13 and again on October 20.

The reports disagree on the date: the Blakely special puts the attack in the early hours of September 29, the Tribune's editorial says "Saturday night" (October 1), and the Cambria Freeman says Sunday morning. Because the Blakely account is the local one and was already in print in Savannah on the morning of October 1, it is the strongest evidence that the killing preceded that weekend. The papers also differ on the victim's first name and on whether he was "taken out" of the jail, as several briefs said, or shot in his cell, as the detailed accounts reported.

reader.title: Lynching of Sandy Wright
bases: A party of masked men took the jail key from the jailer at pistol point and shot a Black prisoner to death in the jail (A1, A2).

About a dozen masked men with no lawful authority forced the jailer to give up the key and shot the prisoner dead (A1, A2); the reports give as the reason his alleged threats to kill the jailer and others on his release, while he was serving a hog-stealing sentence (A1, A3).

The two detailed accounts (A1, A2) share wording and details and appear to derive from one Blakely report, and the later items (A3-A10) condense or reprint; the core event is not contradicted, but no independent second account was found.

versions.value: Between 12 and 1 o'clock, 'last night' in a special dated Blakely, September 29 (night of Sept. 28-29)

conflicts.note: A1 is the earliest, local-origin report and was printed on the morning of Saturday, October 1, so the killing preceded that date; the Saturday and Sunday dates appear in later, distant papers, and the Atlanta wire's dateline is garbled ('Oct. 21').
The detailed accounts give Zandy/Sandy; 'Andy' appears only in short summary items.
The detailed accounts place the shooting inside the jail (A1, A2); 'taken out' appears only in brief summaries.

record_check.dossier: Early hours of September 29, 1881, per the Blakely special dated that day (A1); later papers say Saturday night or Sunday morning (A3, A4).
Named Zandy (A1) or Sandy (A2, A3) Wright in the detailed accounts; Andy only in briefs (A4, A5). The record's own summary says Sandy.
Serving a sentence for hog stealing (already convicted), with about ten days left; the stated reason for the killing was his alleged threats to kill the jailer and others.
The jail key was seized from the jailer, who was held under guard; the prisoner was shot in his cell, not removed, in the detailed accounts (A1, A2), though briefs say 'taken out' (A4, A6).
